questions.question: Financial emergency provisions of the Indian Constitution have been borrowed from ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitution of Germany**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The provision relating to **Financial Emergency (Article 360)** in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the **Constitution of Germany (Weimar Constitution)**.
 
• A Financial Emergency can be proclaimed by the President if the **financial stability or credit of India or any part thereof is threatened**.
 
• During a Financial Emergency, the Union Government can issue directions to states regarding financial matters.
 
• The President may also direct a reduction in the salaries and allowances of government employees, including judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
• Notably, **no Financial Emergency has been declared in India so far**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Canadian Constitution**:

 
 
• Inspired provisions such as the **strong Centre**, appointment of state governors by the Centre, and advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Irish Constitution**:
 
 
• Inspired the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha, and the method of election of the President.
 
 
 
• **American Constitution**:
 
 
• Inspired the **Fundamental Rights**, judicial review, independence of the judiciary, and the impeachment process of the President.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 352** – National Emergency.
 
• **Article 356** – President's Rule / State Emergency.
 
• **Article 360** – Financial Emergency.
 
• **Financial Emergency provision borrowed from Germany (Weimar Constitution)**.
 
• **No Financial Emergency has been imposed in India till date.**

questions.question: A person takes a loan of Rs. 300 at 10% simple interest. He returns Rs. 60 at the end of 1 year. In order to clear his dues at the end of 2ⁿd year he would pay :
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

1st year SI = 10% of ₹300 = ₹30

Total paid after 1 year = ₹60

Remaining principal for 2nd year = 300 − 60 = ₹240

2nd year amount = 240 + 30 + 24 = ₹294

**∴ The correct answer is ₹294.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal = ₹300

Rate of simple interest = 10%

Amount returned after 1 year = ₹60

**Formula Used:**

SI = P × R × T ÷ 100

 
• Start ₹300 After 1 Year Paid ₹60 2nd Year Due ₹294 New Principal = ₹240 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 1 year = 300 × 10 × 1 ÷ 100 = ₹30

⇒ Amount paid at end of 1 year = ₹60

⇒ Principal for 2nd year = 300 − 60 = ₹240

⇒ Interest for 2nd year = 240 × 10 × 1 ÷ 100 = ₹24

⇒ Amount to clear dues at end of 2nd year = 240 + 30 + 24 = ₹294

**∴ The correct answer is ₹294.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = P × R × T ÷ 100 where P = Principal, R = Rate and T = Time.

Part Payment Rule

In some exam questions, the returned amount is directly deducted from principal for the next year calculation.

Difference Between SI and CI

In simple interest, interest is not added to principal for future interest calculation, unlike compound interest.

Mistake Point

Here second year interest is calculated on ₹240, not ₹270. The ₹30 first-year interest is not added again in simple interest.

questions.question: A thief noticing a policeman from a distance of 500 metres starts running at a speed of 8 km/h. The policeman chased him with a speed of 11 km/h. What is the distance run by the thief before he was caught? (Rounded off to two decimal places, if required)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **time** is constant, **distance** is directly proportional to **speed**.

Speed Ratio (Policeman : Thief) = 11 : 8

Distance Ratio (Policeman : Thief) = 11 : 8

Difference in distance ratio parts = 11 − 8 = 3 units → 500 m

Distance run by thief = (8 ÷ 3) × 500 = 4000 ÷ 3 = 1333.33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1,333.33 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial distance = 500 m, Speed of thief (Vₜ) = 8 km/h, Speed of policeman (Vₚ) = 11 km/h.

**Formula Used:** Relative Speed = Vₚ − Vₜ | Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed | Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62e5ee22ec334ba23d8315cbdeb4a7790c25d9d6780d1185848ca8d7d65178c0.png] 

⇒ Relative Speed = 11 − 8 = 3 km/h

⇒ 3 km/h in m/s = 3 × (5/18) = 5/6 m/s

⇒ Time to catch = Initial distance ÷ Relative Speed = 500 ÷ (5/6) = (500 × 6) ÷ 5 = 600 seconds

⇒ Speed of thief in m/s = 8 × (5/18) = 20/9 m/s

⇒ Distance run by thief = Speed × Time = (20/9) × 600

⇒ Distance = 12000 ÷ 9 = 4000 ÷ 3 = 1333.33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1,333.33 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds (V₁ − V₂).

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by **5/18**. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by **18/5**.

Proportionality in Motion

If time is constant, **Distance₁/Distance₂ = Speed₁/Speed₂**. This is the most efficient way to solve chase problems.</p

questions.question: The efficiencies of A, B, and C are in the ratio 5 ∶ 3 ∶ 2. Working together, they can complete a task in 21 hours. In how many hours will B alone complete 40% of that task?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total combined efficiency = 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 units/hour.

Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Total Time = 10 × 21 = 210 units.

Work to be completed by B = 40% of Total Work = 0.40 × 210 = 84 units.

Time required by B alone = Target Work ÷ Efficiency of B = 84 ÷ 3 = 28 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Efficiency ratio of A, B, and C = 5 : 3 : 2

Time taken by (A + B + C) together = 21 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiencies of A, B, and C be 5, 3, and 2 units/hour respectively.

⇒ Combined efficiency of A, B, and C = 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 units/hour

⇒ Total Work = Combined efficiency × Time = 10 × 21 = 210 units

Work and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of efficiency of A and B is x : y, the ratio of time taken by them to complete the same work will be y : x.

Division of Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If they work for the same duration, wages are distributed in the direct ratio of their efficiencies.

questions.question: If the number 22144 is divided in the ratio (1)/(3) ∶ (3)/(5) ∶ (5)/(7), the difference between the largest and smallest part is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Simplify **Ratio** by multiplying by LCM(3, 5, 7) = 105: (1/3 × 105) : (3/5 × 105) : (5/7 × 105) = 35 : 63 : 75.

**Total units** = 35 + 63 + 75 = 173 units.

**Total Value** = 22144 ⇒ 1 unit = 22144 ÷ 173 = 128.

Difference between **Largest** (75) and **Smallest** (35) = 75 − 35 = 40 units.

Required Difference = 40 × 128 = 5120.

**∴ The correct answer is 5120.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Total Number** = 22144

**Ratio** = 1/3 : 3/5 : 5/7

**Formula Used:**

Value of a part = (Ratio of part ÷ Sum of ratios) × Total Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d8d138c85d3dfb86f43d73f746a2d61b1ef320ec3492691e413919db227f826.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simplifying the ratio by finding LCM of 3, 5, and 7:

⇒ LCM(3, 5, 7) = 105

⇒ New Ratio = (1/3 × 105) : (3/5 × 105) : (5/7 × 105) = 35 : 63 : 75

⇒ Let the three parts be 35x, 63x, and 75x

⇒ 35x + 63x + 75x = 22144

⇒ 173x = 22144

⇒ x = 22144 ÷ 173 = 128

⇒ Smallest part = 35x = 35 × 128 = 4480

⇒ Largest part = 75x = 75 × 128 = 9600

⇒ Required Difference = 9600 − 4480 = 5120

**∴ The correct answer is 5120.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio Normalization

To convert a fractional ratio a/b : c/d : e/f into an integer ratio, multiply each term by the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the denominators (b, d, f).

Direct Difference Calculation

Instead of calculating individual parts, the difference can be found directly using the formula: Difference = (Difference in ratio parts ÷ Sum of ratio parts) × Total Value.

Property of Proportion

If a : b : c is the ratio of three quantities whose sum is S, then the parts are S × a/(a+b+c), S × b/(a+b+c), and S × c/(a+b+c).</p

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When a solid is melted, Volume of Cube = Volume of Cuboid

⇒ (6 × ³√4)³ = 12 × 9 × h

⇒ 216 × 4 = 108 × h ⇒ h = 8 cm

Longest diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²) = √(12² + 9² + 8²)

⇒ Longest diagonal = √(144 + 81 + 64) = √289 = 17 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the cube (a) = 6 × ³√4 cm

Length of the cuboid (l) = 12 cm

Breadth of the cuboid (b) = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cube = a³

Volume of a cuboid = l × b × h

Longest diagonal of a cuboid = √(l² + b² + h²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88709803b125899499f82a7816a8fc2ee8bc2c2786389592bbd1a914e2926a58.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since the solid metallic cube is melted and recast into a cuboid, their volumes will be equal.

⇒ Volume of Cube = Volume of Cuboid

⇒ a³ = l × b × h

⇒ (6 × ³√4)³ = 12 × 9 × h

⇒ 6³ × (³√4)³ = 108 × h

⇒ 216 × 4 = 108 × h

⇒ 864 = 108 × h

⇒ h = 864 ÷ 108

⇒ h = 8 cm

Now, substitute the values of l, b, and h to find the length of the longest diagonal:

⇒ Longest diagonal = √(12² + 9² + 8²)

⇒ Longest diagonal = √(144 + 81 + 64)

⇒ Longest diagonal = √289

⇒ Longest diagonal = 17 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 17 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Melting and Recasting

When any 3D solid is melted to form a new solid, the total mass and volume remain perfectly conserved. (Volume of original solid = Volume of new solid)

Properties of a Cube

Volume = a³ | Total Surface Area = 6a² | Body Diagonal = a√3

Properties of a Cuboid

Volume = l × b × h | Total Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl) | Longest Diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²)

questions.question: A dishonest delivery man purchases 20 liters of pure milk and dilutes it by adding 4 liters of water. If he sells the diluted milk at Rs. 50/L, then what is the cost price of pure milk?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total quantity of diluted milk = 20 L + 4 L = 24 L.

Total revenue from selling diluted milk = 24 L × Rs. 50/L = Rs. 1200.

To have no profit/loss, total **Cost Price** of 20 L pure milk must equal the total revenue.

**Cost Price** of pure milk = 1200 ÷ 20 = Rs. 60/L.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 60/L.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity of **Pure Milk** = 20 L

Quantity of **Water Added** = 4 L

**Selling Price** (SP) of diluted milk = Rs. 50/L

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca3baaf56d56cefce77735b9ee235228777be378283ccdf9a07fde5b8ec7d3e3.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total Revenue = Total Quantity × Selling Price per unit

Cost Price per unit = Total Cost ÷ Original Quantity

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total volume of mixture = 20 + 4 = 24 L

⇒ Total **Selling Price** (SP) = 24 × 50 = Rs. 1200

⇒ Since water is free and profit/loss is not mentioned, **Total Cost** of milk = Total SP

⇒ Total **Cost Price** (CP) of 20 L milk = Rs. 1200

⇒ **Cost Price** per liter of pure milk = 1200 ÷ 20 = Rs. 60/L

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 60/L.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage in Adulteration

If a milkman sells diluted milk at the **Cost Price** of pure milk, his profit % is (Quantity of Water ÷ Quantity of Milk) × 100.

Alligation Rule

The ratio of quantities of two ingredients is (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper).

Cost of Water

In mathematical aptitude problems, the **Cost Price** of water added to milk is always assumed to be zero unless specified otherwise.</p

questions.question: If { X} = 3 + 2sqrt 2 , x > 0, then the value of sqrt { X} - (1)/({sqrt { X) }} is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **y = √x − 1/√x**.

Squaring both sides gives: **y² = x + 1/x − 2**

Given **x = 3 + 2√2**, its reciprocal is **1/x = 3 − 2√2**.

Substitute these into the equation: **y² = (3 + 2√2) + (3 − 2√2) − 2**

⇒ y² = 6 − 2 = 4 ⇒ y = 2 (since x > 1, y must be positive).

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **x = 3 + 2√2**

⇒ **x > 0**

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab**

⇒ **(a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²**

**Calculations:**

Expressing the given value of **x** as a perfect square:

⇒ x = 2 + 1 + 2√2

⇒ x = (√2)² + (1)² + 2 × (√2) × (1)

⇒ x = (√2 + 1)²

Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ √x = √2 + 1

Now, find the value of reciprocal term **1/√x**:

⇒ 1/√x = 1/(√2 + 1)

Rationalizing the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator by **(√2 − 1)**:

⇒ 1/√x = (1 × (√2 − 1)) / ((√2 + 1)(√2 − 1))

⇒ 1/√x = (√2 − 1) / (2 − 1)

⇒ 1/√x = √2 − 1

Now, substitute the values of **√x** and **1/√x** into the required expression:

⇒ √x − 1/√x = (√2 + 1) − (√2 − 1)

⇒ √x − 1/√x = √2 + 1 − √2 + 1

⇒ √x − 1/√x = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of a Surd

To find the square root of a binomial quadratic surd of the form **a + 2√b**, we find two numbers whose sum is **a** and whose product is **b**. The square root is then given by **√x + √y**.

Rationalization Conjugate

For any expression of the form **√a + √b**, its rationalizing factor is **√a − √b**. Multiplying them results in a rational number **a − b**.

Identity for Reciprocals

If **x = a + √b** and **a² − b = 1**, then the reciprocal is always **1/x = a − √b**.</p

questions.question: In a ΔABC, if ∠A = 90°, AC = 5 cm, BC = 9 cm, and in ΔPQR, ∠P = 90°, PR = 3 cm, QR = 8 cm, then:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Compare corresponding parts of right-angled ΔABC and ΔPQR.

In ΔABC: Hypotenuse BC = 9 cm and Side AC = 5 cm.

In ΔPQR: Hypotenuse QR = 8 cm and Side PR = 3 cm.

Congruence (RHS) requires Hypotenuse 1 = Hypotenuse 2 and Side 1 = Side 2.

Since 9 ≠ 8 and 5 ≠ 3, the triangles cannot be congruent.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔABC ≇ ΔPQR.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC: ∠A = 90°, AC = 5 cm, BC = 9 cm (Hypotenuse)

ΔPQR: ∠P = 90°, PR = 3 cm, QR = 8 cm (Hypotenuse)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89b0ac819db213682b3bf2149aa361401a41fe3ddac32e59e458778a5e09dee8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side) Congruence Rule: Two right-angled triangles are congruent if the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and the corresponding side of the other triangle.

⇒ In ΔABC, using Pythagoras theorem: AB² = BC² − AC²

⇒ AB² = 9² − 5² = 81 − 25 = 56
⇒ AB = √56 cm ≈ 7.48 cm

⇒ In ΔPQR, using Pythagoras theorem: PQ² = QR² − PR²

⇒ PQ² = 8² − 3² = 64 − 9 = 55
⇒ PQ = √55 cm ≈ 7.41 cm

⇒ Comparing the dimensions of ΔABC and ΔPQR:

⇒ Hypotenuse: BC (9 cm) ≠ QR (8 cm)
⇒ Side 1: AC (5 cm) ≠ PR (3 cm)
⇒ Side 2: AB (√56 cm) ≠ PQ (√55 cm)

⇒ Since none of the corresponding sides are equal, the triangles are not congruent.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔABC ≇ ΔPQR.**

**__Additional Information__**

RHS Congruence Rule

If in two right-angled triangles, the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and one side of the other triangle, then the two triangles are congruent.

SSS Congruence Rule

Two triangles are congruent if all three sides of one triangle are equal to the corresponding three sides of the other triangle.

Congruence vs. Equality

Congruent triangles (≅) have the exact same shape and size (identical sides and angles), whereas equal triangles (=) usually refers to triangles having equal area even if shapes differ.</p

questions.question: The cost of diamond is directly proportional to the square of its weight. The cost of diamond is Rs. 69660. It break into two pieces whose weight are in the ratio of 4 : 5. What is the loss incurred because of the breakage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The cost of the diamond is directly proportional to the square of its weight.

Total cost of the diamond = Rs. 69660

The diamond breaks into two pieces in the ratio 4:5.

We need to calculate the loss incurred due to the breakage.

**Concept:**

1. If cost (C) is directly proportional to the square of weight (W), then:

C = k × W², where k is the proportionality constant.

2. Loss due to breakage = Original cost - (Cost of first piece + Cost of second piece).

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Let the total weight of the diamond be W.

The weight of the first piece = (4/9) × W

The weight of the second piece = (5/9) × W

Step 2: Find the proportionality constant (k).

Total cost = k × W²

69660 = k × W²

k = 69660 / W²

Step 3: Calculate the cost of each piece.

Cost of the first piece = k × (4/9 × W)²

= (69660 / W²) × (16/81) × W²

= 69660 × 16 / 81

= Rs. 13760

Cost of the second piece = k × (5/9 × W)²

= (69660 / W²) × (25/81) × W²

= 69660 × 25 / 81

= Rs. 21500

Total cost after breakage = Rs. 13760 + Rs. 21500 = Rs. 35260

Step 4: Calculate the loss incurred.

Loss = Original cost - Total cost after breakage

Loss = Rs. 69660 - Rs. 35260

Loss = Rs. 34400

**Therefore, the loss incurred because of the breakage is Rs. 34400.**

D's total investment = 5 × 3 = 15 unit

Since, the profit is directly proportional to the total investment.

**Therefore, C would receive the highest amount of profit.**

questions.solution:
**Given**:

The roots of the equation (b - c)x2 + (c - a)x + (a - b) = 0 are equal.

**Concept**:

For any given quadratic equation of the form px² + qx + r = 0 having equal roots then,

q² - 4pr = 0

**Solution**:

According to the question,

The quadratic equation is as follows,

(b - c)x2 + (c - a)x + (a - b) = 0 

p = (b - c)

q = (c - a)

r = (a - b)

Now,

q2 - 4pr = 0

(c - a)² - 4(b - c)(a - b) = 0

c² + a² - 2ac - 4(ba - b² - ac + bc) = 0

c2 + a2 + 4b2 - 4ab + 2ac - 4bc = 0

( a + c - 2b )² = 0

a + c - 2b = 0

a + c = 2b

The correct answer is __**Improve accuracy and reduce tampering**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Digitizing evidence collection** under the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (Indian Evidence Act)** aims to **improve accuracy** in the handling of evidence, ensuring that the collected data remains authentic and untampered.
 
• By digitizing evidence collection, the process ensures a **secure chain of custody**, reducing the risk of manual errors or manipulation during the handling of evidence.
 
• **Electronic evidence**, such as digital recordings, documents, or multimedia files, can be timestamped and stored securely, making it more reliable in legal proceedings.
 
• Digitization helps eliminate the risks of **physical damage or loss** of evidence, as digital records are easier to store and retrieve compared to physical copies.
 
• The initiative aligns with the broader goal of modernizing India's legal system by integrating **technology and transparency** into judicial processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (Indian Evidence Act):**

 
 
• The **Indian Evidence Act** was enacted in **1872** and provides the legal framework for the admissibility of evidence in courts.
 
• It lays out rules regarding the **presentation, collection, and validation** of evidence during legal proceedings.
 
• The Act has provisions for handling **electronic evidence**, including emails, digital photographs, and electronic contracts, which are increasingly relevant in the modern era.
 
• Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act governs the **admissibility of electronic records**, ensuring that they meet specific criteria for authenticity.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Evidence Collection:**
 
 
• Traditional methods of evidence collection often face issues such as **tampering, loss, or delays** in submission.
 
• Manual handling of evidence can lead to human errors, compromising the reliability of the evidence presented in court.
 
• Digitization addresses these challenges by offering **secure and efficient storage and transfer mechanisms**.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Digitized Evidence Collection:**
 
 
• It ensures better compliance with **legal standards** for admissibility and accuracy.
 
• Digital evidence can be stored in **encrypted formats**, making it secure against unauthorized access or tampering.
 
• Modern tools such as **blockchain** can be used to establish a tamper-proof record of evidence.
 
• Digitization promotes **transparency and trust** in judicial processes by minimizing the scope for manipulation.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Digitization in Legal Systems:**
 
 
• Countries like the **United States** and the **United Kingdom** have adopted digital systems for evidence collection and courtroom procedures.
 
• In India, initiatives such as the **e-Courts project** aim to digitize court records and improve accessibility to legal resources.
 
• The use of **digital forensics** in criminal investigations is increasingly common, allowing authorities to recover and analyze electronic evidence effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act:**

 
 
• This section provides guidelines for the **admissibility of electronic records** as evidence in legal proceedings.
 
• It requires electronic records to be certified, ensuring that they are authentic and reliable.
 
• Courts have emphasized the importance of adhering to Section 65B for the admissibility of digital evidence.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Modernization in India:**
 
 
• The **e-Courts Mission Mode Project** aims to modernize the judiciary by digitizing court records, case management systems, and evidence handling.
 
• These initiatives are part of the **Digital India campaign**, focusing on leveraging technology to improve governance and public services.
 
• Digitization of evidence collection is a key step in achieving faster and more efficient judicial processes.

• The mission primarily focuses on two aspects: **Area-based development** (ABD) and **Pan-city initiatives**.

• Examples include smart water management systems, intelligent traffic management, and waste management solutions.

questions.question: Two pillars A and B of the same height are on opposite sides of a road which is 40 m wide. The angles of elevation of the tops of the pillars A and B are 30° and 45°, respectively, at a point on the road between the pillars. What is the distance (in m) of the point from the foot of pillar A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height is same for both pillars, so use ratio method.

For 30°, height : base = 1 : √3. For 45°, height : base = 1 : 1.

Total road width = Sum of bases = (√3 + 1) units.

Given √3 + 1 units = 40 m ⇒ 1 unit = 40 / (√3 + 1) m.

Distance from A (base of 30°) = √3 units = 40√3 / (√3 + 1) m.

Rationalizing: 40√3(√3 − 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = 20(3 − √3) m.

**∴ The correct answer is 20(3−√3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Width of road = 40 m

Height of pillar A = Height of pillar B = h

Angle of elevation of A = 30°

Angle of elevation of B = 45°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Height / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3acbc4d4d48c245fe8efec86e47ff6b3797df96f0e1d1d93459fe159abbb47d.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the distance of the point P from pillar A (A') be x m.

Then, the distance of the point P from pillar B (B') = (40 − x) m.

In ΔAA'P:

⇒ tan 30° = h / x

⇒ 1 / √3 = h / x

⇒ h = x / √3 ---- (1)

In ΔBB'P:

⇒ tan 45° = h / (40 − x)

⇒ 1 = h / (40 − x)

⇒ h = 40 − x ---- (2)

Equating (1) and (2):

⇒ x / √3 = 40 − x

⇒ x = 40√3 − x√3

⇒ x(1 + √3) = 40√3

⇒ x = 40√3 / (√3 + 1)

⇒ x = [40√3 / (√3 + 1)] × [(√3 − 1) / (√3 − 1)]

⇒ x = [40√3(√3 − 1)] / (3 − 1)

⇒ x = [40(3 − √3)] / 2

⇒ x = 20(3 − √3) m

**∴ The correct answer is 20(3−√3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

For height and distance, remember tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Rationalization of Denominator

To simplify fractions with surds like a / (√b + c), multiply both numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√b − c).

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking up at an object. It equals the angle of depression from the object to the point.</p
